points.title: A その上 B (A sono ue B)
points.meaning: Used to express 'in addition to', 'besides', or 'furthermore' when adding information or making a suggestion.
points.explanation: The grammar point A その上 B is used to connect two statements, where B is an additional piece of information, a suggestion or reason that is related to statement A. The expression can be translated as 'in addition to', 'besides', or 'furthermore'.
points.short: Used to express 'in addition to', 'besides', or 'furthermore' when adding information or making a suggestion.
points.long: The grammar point A その上 B is used to connect two statements, where B is an additional piece of information, a suggestion or reason that is related to statement A. The expression can be translated as 'in addition to', 'besides', or 'furthermore'.
formation: A [sentence/clause] + その上 + B [sentence/clause]

examples.jp: 彼は頭が良い。その上、スポーツも得意だ。
examples.ja: 彼は頭が良い。その上、スポーツも得意だ。
examples.romaji: Kare wa atama ga ii. Sono ue, supootsu mo tokui da.
examples.en: He is smart. On top of that, he is good at sports.
examples.literalEn: He is smart. In addition, he is also good at sports.
examples.naturalEn: He is smart. On top of that, he is good at sports.

examples.jp: このカフェは雰囲気がいい。その上、料理も美味しい。
examples.ja: このカフェは雰囲気がいい。その上、料理も美味しい。
examples.romaji: Kono kafe wa fun'iki ga ii. Sono ue, ryouri mo oishii.
examples.en: This café has a great atmosphere. On top of that, the food is delicious.

cloze.before: このカフェは雰囲気がいい。

examples.literalEn: This cafe has a nice atmosphere. Besides, the food is delicious.
examples.naturalEn: This café has a great atmosphere. On top of that, the food is delicious.

examples.jp: このアパートは駅に近い。その上、家賃も安い。
examples.ja: このアパートは駅に近い。その上、家賃も安い。
examples.romaji: Kono apaato wa eki ni chikai. Sono ue, yachin mo yasui.
examples.en: This apartment is close to the station. On top of that, the rent is cheap.

cloze.before: このアパートは駅に近い。

examples.literalEn: This apartment is close to the station. Furthermore, the rent is also cheap.
examples.naturalEn: This apartment is close to the station. On top of that, the rent is cheap.

examples.jp: 彼女は仕事ができる。その上、誰とでも仲良くなれる。
examples.ja: 彼女は仕事ができる。その上、誰とでも仲良くなれる。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa shigoto ga dekiru. Sono ue, dare to demo nakayoku nareru.
examples.en: She is good at her job. On top of that, she gets along well with everyone.
examples.literalEn: She is competent at work. In addition, she can get along with anyone.
examples.naturalEn: She is good at her job. On top of that, she gets along well with everyone.

examples.jp: リンクを開くには、その上でダブルクリックしてください。
examples.ja: リンクを開くには、その上でダブルクリックしてください。
examples.romaji: Rinku o hiraku ni wa, sono ue de daburu kurikku shite kudasai
examples.en: To open a link, double-click on it.
chunks: クリックしてください。

cloze.after: でダブルクリックしてください。

examples.literalEn: To open the link, please double click on it.
examples.naturalEn: To open a link, double-click on it.

notes.nuance: The expression “A その上 B” is used to express “in addition to,” “besides,” or “furthermore” when adding information or making a suggestion. It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, “A, and furthermore, B” clearly indicates the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of mistakes in conjugation when using the "on top of that" construction (A [sentence/clause] + その上 + B [sentence/clause]). It is important to use the dictionary form and the "te" form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～うちに (〜uchi ni)
points.meaning: Express 'while', 'before', or 'during' a certain condition or situation.
points.explanation: The ～うちに grammar point is used to express the idea of doing something while a certain condition or situation is still present or before it changes. It can be translated as 'while', 'before', or 'during' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, or な-adjective.
points.short: Express 'while', 'before', or 'during' a certain condition or situation.
points.long: The ～うちに grammar point is used to express the idea of doing something while a certain condition or situation is still present or before it changes. It can be translated as 'while', 'before', or 'during' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, or な-adjective.
formation: Verb-てform + いる + うちに, い-Adjective + い + うちに, な-Adjective + な + うちに

examples.jp: 若いうちに、いろいろな経験をしておくことが大切です。

examples.ja: この料理は熱いうちに食べるべきです。

notes.nuance: The expression “～うちに” is used to express “while,” “before,” or “during” a certain condition or situation. It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, “～うちに” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the “-te” form + “-iru” + “-uchi” construction, as well as in the “-i” adjective + “-i” + “-uchi” and “-na” adjective + “-na” + “-uchi” constructions. points.title: ～うとした (〜uto shita)
points.meaning: Express an action someone tried to do but couldn't; 'tried to', 'attempted to'.
points.explanation: The ～うとした grammar point is used to express an action that someone tried to do but couldn't complete, for various reasons. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with verbs. This grammar point can be translated as 'tried to' or 'attempted to' in English.
points.short: Express an action someone tried to do but couldn't; 'tried to', 'attempted to'.
points.long: The ～うとした grammar point is used to express an action that someone tried to do but couldn't complete, for various reasons. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with verbs. This grammar point can be translated as 'tried to' or 'attempted to' in English.
formation: Verb-う stem + とした

examples.jp: 電話に出ようとしたが、相手は切ってしまった。
examples.ja: 電話に出ようとしたが、相手は切ってしまった。

notes.nuance: The expression “～うとした” means “to express an action someone tried to do but couldn’t; ‘tried to,’ ‘attempted to.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective descriptions and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～うとした” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intention or focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful not to make mistakes in the conjugation of the "tsunage" form (Verb-u-stem + -tashita). It is important to use the dictionary form and the "te" form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～おかげで (〜okagede)
points.meaning: Expresses gratitude or shows a positive result due to a certain factor; 'thanks to', 'because of'.
points.explanation: The ～おかげで grammar point is used to express gratitude or show a positive outcome resulting from a certain factor, event or person. It can be translated as 'thanks to' or 'because of' in English. The formation is straightforward and can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
points.short: Expresses gratitude or shows a positive result due to a certain factor; 'thanks to', 'because of'.
points.long: The ～おかげで grammar point is used to express gratitude or show a positive outcome resulting from a certain factor, event or person. It can be translated as 'thanks to' or 'because of' in English. The formation is straightforward and can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
formation: Verb-casual + おかげで, い-Adjective + おかげで, な-Adjective + だおかげで, Noun + のおかげで

notes.nuance: The expression “～おかげで” means “Expresses gratitude or shows a positive result due to a certain factor; ‘thanks to,’ ‘because of.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.

points.title: ～かけ (〜kake)
points.meaning: Expresses the meaning of being in the middle of doing something or of something being partway done.
points.explanation: The ～かけ grammar point is used to indicate that something is in the process of being done or is partway completed. This is often used with verbs to describe an action that is not yet finished or is ongoing. The verb should be in its ます-form, and かけ is added after removing the ます.
points.short: Expresses the meaning of being in the middle of doing something or of something being partway done.
points.long: The ～かけ grammar point is used to indicate that something is in the process of being done or is partway completed. This is often used with verbs to describe an action that is not yet finished or is ongoing. The verb should be in its ます-form, and かけ is added after removing the ます.
formation: Verb-ますstem + かけ

examples.jp: 彼は食事を食べかけです。
examples.ja: 彼は食事を食べかけです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shokuji wo tabekake desu.

notes.nuance: The expression “～かけ” conveys the meaning of “being in the middle of doing something or of something being partway done.” It is an important grammatical point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, “～かけ” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful not to make mistakes in the conjugation of the “tsunage” form (Verb-masu stem + kake). It is important to use the dictionary form and the “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～かなあ (〜kanaa)
points.meaning: Expressing uncertainty or a mild wish; 'I wonder', 'maybe'.
points.explanation: The ～かなあ grammar point is used to express uncertainty or a mild wish. It can be translated as 'I wonder' or 'maybe' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
points.short: Expressing uncertainty or a mild wish; 'I wonder', 'maybe'.
points.long: The ～かなあ grammar point is used to express uncertainty or a mild wish. It can be translated as 'I wonder' or 'maybe' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + かなあ, い-Adjective + かなあ, な-Adjective + だかなあ, Noun + だかなあ

points.title: ～から～にかけて (〜kara 〜ni kakete)

points.title: ～きり (〜kiri)
points.meaning: Expresses the idea of 'only', 'since', or 'after'.
points.explanation: The ～きり grammar point is used to express the idea of 'only', 'since', or 'after'. It indicates that a certain action or state continues without any change since a specific point in time or after a certain event. It is commonly used with verbs in the past tense, but can also be used with other forms.

points.title: ～こそ (〜koso)
points.meaning: Emphasizes the importance or uniqueness of something or someone; 'precisely', 'exactly', 'it is...', 'of all...'.
points.explanation: The ～こそ grammar point is used to emphasize the importance, uniqueness, or the most suitable thing or person in a specific situation. It can be translated as 'precisely', 'exactly', or 'it is...' in English. In practice, it most often appears after a noun (e.g. 今日こそ), or with verbs in the て-form (e.g. 頑張ってこそ).
points.short: Emphasizes the importance or uniqueness of something or someone; 'precisely', 'exactly', 'it is...', 'of all...'.
points.long: The ～こそ grammar point is used to emphasize the importance, uniqueness, or the most suitable thing or person in a specific situation. It can be translated as 'precisely', 'exactly', or 'it is...' in English. In practice, it most often appears after a noun (e.g. 今日こそ), or with verbs in the て-form (e.g. 頑張ってこそ).

points.title: ～こと (〜koto)
points.meaning: Express an action in a nominal (noun-like) form or state fact or experience.
points.explanation: The ～こと grammar point is used to turn a verb or verb phrase into a noun or noun phrase. This allows the verb to be talked about as a general concept, fact, or experience. The formation varies slightly depending on whether it is used with a verb or a verb phrase.

points.long: The ～こと grammar point is used to turn a verb or verb phrase into a noun or noun phrase. This allows the verb to be talked about as a general concept, fact, or experience. The formation varies slightly depending on whether it is used with a verb or a verb phrase.

points.title: ～ことにしている (〜koto ni shite iru)
points.meaning: Express a personal rule or habit; 'I make it a rule to', 'I always make sure to'.
points.explanation: The ～ことにしている grammar point is used to express a personal rule, habit, or decision that the speaker has made for themselves. It can be translated as 'I make it a rule to' or 'I always make sure to' in English. This grammar point is formed by attaching ことにしている to the casual form of a verb.

points.title: ～せてください (〜sete kudasai)
points.meaning: Requesting someone to allow or let you do something (causative request).
points.explanation: The せてください grammar point is used to request permission or ask someone to allow you to do something. It is a polite way of making a request and can be translated as 'please let me...' or 'please allow me...' in English. It is formed by using the causative form of the verb (Verb-させる) in the て-form, plus ください (e.g. 帰らせる → 帰らせて → 帰らせてください).
points.short: Requesting someone to allow or let you do something (causative request).
points.long: The せてください grammar point is used to request permission or ask someone to allow you to do something. It is a polite way of making a request and can be translated as 'please let me...' or 'please allow me...' in English. It is formed by using the causative form of the verb (Verb-させる) in the て-form, plus ください (e.g. 帰らせる → 帰らせて → 帰らせてください).

points.title: ～そのために (〜sono tame ni)
points.meaning: For the purpose of; because of; in order to.
points.explanation: The ～そのために grammar point is used to convey the purpose or reason behind an action or situation. It can be translated as 'for that reason', 'for the purpose of', or 'in order to' in English. It connects two sentences, where the first sentence gives a goal or reason, and the second sentence shows the resulting action.
points.short: For the purpose of; because of; in order to.
points.long: The ～そのために grammar point is used to convey the purpose or reason behind an action or situation. points.title: ～その結果 (〜sono kekka)
points.meaning: Shows the result or consequence of a previous action or situation; 'as a result', 'in consequence'.
points.explanation: The ～その結果 grammar point is used to show the result, outcome, or consequence of a previous action or situation. It can be translated as 'as a result', 'in consequence', or 'therefore' in English. It is typically placed between two statements to link cause and effect.

points.title: ～それと～ (〜sore to〜)
points.meaning: Used to link two or more items; 'and', 'also'.
points.explanation: The ～それと～ grammar point is used to connect two or more items or actions, similar to how 'and' or 'also' is used in English. The expression それと can appear at the start of a new sentence or between items in a list to add another point.
points.short: Used to link two or more items; 'and', 'also'.
points.long: The ～それと～ grammar point is used to connect two or more items or actions, similar to how 'and' or 'also' is used in English. The expression それと can appear at the start of a new sentence or between items in a list to add another point.

points.title: だけど (dakedo)
points.meaning: Expresses a contrast or contradiction; 'but', 'however', 'even though'.
points.explanation: The だけど grammar point is used to express a contrast or contradiction between two statements. In written or spoken Japanese, だけど is often placed at the start of a new sentence (after a period) to mean 'however'. Within a single sentence, speakers often just say けど without だ.
points.short: Expresses a contrast or contradiction; 'but', 'however', 'even though'.
points.long: The だけど grammar point is used to express a contrast or contradiction between two statements. In written or spoken Japanese, だけど is often placed at the start of a new sentence (after a period) to mean 'however'. Within a single sentence, speakers often just say けど without だ.

points.title: ～たて (～tate)
points.meaning: Indicates an action that has just been completed; 'freshly', 'just'.
points.explanation: The ～たて grammar point is used to express that an action has just been completed, and the result or condition is still fresh or new. This is often used with verbs like 焼く (bake), 作る (make), or 洗う (wash).
points.short: Indicates an action that has just been completed; 'freshly', 'just'.
points.long: The ～たて grammar point is used to express that an action has just been completed, and the result or condition is still fresh or new. This is often used with verbs like 焼く (bake), 作る (make), or 洗う (wash).

points.title: ～たとえ～ても (〜tatoe〜temo)
points.meaning: Express a condition with 'even if'; 'no matter how'.
points.explanation: The ～たとえ～ても grammar point is used to express a hypothetical or conditional situation where the outcome remains the same even if the condition is met. It can be translated as 'even if' or 'no matter how' in English.
points.short: Express a condition with 'even if'; 'no matter how'.
points.long: The ～たとえ～ても grammar point is used to express a hypothetical or conditional situation where the outcome remains the same even if the condition is met. It can be translated as 'even if' or 'no matter how' in English.

points.title: ～たところ (〜ta tokoro)
points.meaning: Expresses the result or outcome of an action; 'after', 'just when', 'upon'.
points.explanation: The ～たところ grammar point is used to indicate the result or outcome right after performing an action. It can be translated as 'after', 'just when', or 'upon' in English. It is formed by attaching ところ to the past tense (た-form) of verbs.
points.short: Expresses the result or outcome of an action; 'after', 'just when', 'upon'.
points.long: The ～たところ grammar point is used to indicate the result or outcome right after performing an action. It can be translated as 'after', 'just when', or 'upon' in English. It is formed by attaching ところ to the past tense (た-form) of verbs.

points.title: ～たとたん (〜ta totan)
points.meaning: Express the moment something happens; 'as soon as', 'the moment', 'the instant'.
points.explanation: The ～たとたん grammar point is used to express that something occurs immediately at the exact moment another action is completed. It can be translated as 'as soon as', 'the moment', or 'the instant' in English. It is attached to the past tense (た-form) of a verb.
points.short: Express the moment something happens; 'as soon as', 'the moment', 'the instant'.
points.long: The ～たとたん grammar point is used to express that something occurs immediately at the exact moment another action is completed. It can be translated as 'as soon as', 'the moment', or 'the instant' in English. It is attached to the past tense (た-form) of a verb.

points.title: ～たびに (〜tabi ni)
points.meaning: Express 'every time' or 'whenever'.

points.explanation: The ～だものだ grammar point is used to explain a reason or cause in a subjective, explanatory tone (e.g. 'because... after all'). Often, you'll see it used as ～だものだから ('because... after all').
points.short: Express the reason or cause, often used to justify something.
points.long: The ～だものだ grammar point is used to explain a reason or cause in a subjective, explanatory tone (e.g. 'because... after all'). Often, you'll see it used as ～だものだから ('because... after all').
formation: Verb-casual + んだものだ, い-Adjective + んだものだ, な-Adjective + なんだものだ, Noun + なんだものだ (often with から as んだものだから)

examples.jp: 疲れたんだものだから、休みたい。
examples.ja: 疲れたんだものだから、休みたい。
examples.romaji: Tsukareta n da mono da kara, yasumitai.
examples.en: I want to rest because I'm tired.

examples.jp: お腹が空いたんだものだから、何か食べたい。
examples.ja: お腹が空いたんだものだから、何か食べたい。
examples.romaji: Onaka ga suita n da mono da kara, nanika tabetai.
examples.en: I’m hungry, so I want to eat something.
chunks: 空いたんだものだから、
examples.literalEn: I want to eat something because I'm hungry.
examples.naturalEn: I’m hungry, so I want to eat something.

examples.jp: 忙しいんだものだから、来られない。
examples.ja: 忙しいんだものだから、来られない。
examples.romaji: Isogashii n da mono da kara, korarenai.
examples.en: I can't come because I'm busy.

examples.jp: 彼は親切なんだものだから、誰も彼が好きだ。
examples.ja: 彼は親切なんだものだから、誰も彼が好きだ。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shinsetsu na n da mono da kara, dare mo kare ga suki da.
examples.en: Since he’s such a kind person, everyone likes him.
chunks: 親切なんだものだから、
examples.literalEn: Everyone likes him because he is kind.
examples.naturalEn: Since he’s such a kind person, everyone likes him.

notes.nuance: The expression “～だものだ” is used to “express the reason or cause, often to justify something.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, “～だものだ” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the “nda-mono” construction (Verb-casual + んだものだ, i-adjective + んだものだ, na-adjective + なんだものだ, noun + なんだものだ (often with から as んだものだから)). It is important to use the dictionary form and te-form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～ちゃった (〜chatta)
points.meaning: Express an unintentional action or a regretful action; 'ended up doing', 'did accidentally'.
points.explanation: The ～ちゃった grammar point is the informal, colloquial version of ～てしまった. It expresses unintentional or regretful actions and can be translated as 'ended up doing' or 'did accidentally'.
points.short: Express an unintentional action or a regretful action; 'ended up doing', 'did accidentally'.
points.long: The ～ちゃった grammar point is the informal, colloquial version of ～てしまった. It expresses unintentional or regretful actions and can be translated as 'ended up doing' or 'did accidentally'.
formation: Verb-て/で form → ちゃった/じゃった (e.g. 食べてしまった → 食べちゃった)

examples.jp: 忘れ物をしちゃった。
examples.ja: 忘れ物をしちゃった。
examples.romaji: Wasuremono o shichatta.
examples.en: I forgot something.
examples.literalEn: I accidentally left something behind.
examples.naturalEn: I forgot something.

examples.jp: 寝坊して遅刻しちゃった。
examples.ja: 寝坊して遅刻しちゃった。
examples.romaji: Nebou shite chikoku shichatta.
examples.en: I overslept and ended up being late.

examples.jp: ケーキを全部食べちゃった。
examples.ja: ケーキを全部食べちゃった。
examples.romaji: Keeki o zenbu tabechatta.
examples.en: I ate the whole cake.
examples.literalEn: I ended up eating the whole cake.
examples.naturalEn: I ate the whole cake.

examples.jp: 言わないつもりだったけど、言っちゃった。
examples.ja: 言わないつもりだったけど、言っちゃった。
examples.romaji: Iwanai tsumori datta kedo, icchatta.
examples.en: I wasn’t planning to say it, but I ended up saying it.
chunks: 言わないつもりだった

cloze.before: 言わないつもりだったけど、言っ

examples.literalEn: I wasn't planning to say it, but I ended up saying it.
examples.naturalEn: I wasn’t planning to say it, but I ended up saying it.

examples.jp: 寝ぼけ眼で髭を剃ろうとして怪我しちゃった。
examples.ja: 寝ぼけ眼で髭を剃ろうとして怪我しちゃった。
examples.romaji: Nebokemana de hige o sorou to shite kega shichatta.
examples.en: I was still half-asleep when I tried to shave and ended up cutting myself.

cloze.before: 寝ぼけ眼で髭を剃ろうとして怪我し

examples.literalEn: I injured myself while trying to shave my beard with sleepy eyes.
examples.naturalEn: I was still half-asleep when I tried to shave and ended up cutting myself.

notes.nuance: The expression “～ちゃった” is used to “express an unintentional action or a regrettable action; ‘ended up doing,’ ‘did accidentally.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, “～ちゃった” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intention or focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors involving the “-cha/ja” ending (Verb-te/de form → -cha/ja form; e.g., “tabete shimatta” → “tabechatta”). It is important to use the dictionary form, the “-te” form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: ～ついでに (〜tsuide ni)
points.meaning: Do something while or after completing another action; 'while', 'by the way'.
points.explanation: The ～ついでに grammar point is used to express doing something 'on the occasion of' another action. It can mean 'while you're at it', 'by the way', or 'in passing'.
points.short: Do something while or after completing another action; 'while', 'by the way'.
points.long: The ～ついでに grammar point is used to express doing something 'on the occasion of' another action. It can mean 'while you're at it', 'by the way', or 'in passing'.
formation: Verb (dictionary or た-form) + ついでに, Noun + の + ついでに, or Verb-て form + いる + ついでに

examples.jp: 買い物に行くついでに、郵便局で手紙を出しましょう。
examples.ja: 買い物に行くついでに、郵便局で手紙を出しましょう。
examples.romaji: Kaimono ni iku tsuide ni, yuubinkyoku de tegami wo dashimashou.
examples.en: While you’re out shopping, why not drop off a letter at the post office?

cloze.after: 、郵便局で手紙を出しましょう。

examples.literalEn: Let's drop off a letter at the post office while going shopping.
examples.naturalEn: While you’re out shopping, why not drop off a letter at the post office?

examples.jp: 図書館で本を借りたついでに、友達に会いました。
examples.ja: 図書館で本を借りたついでに、友達に会いました。
examples.romaji: Toshokan de hon wo karita tsuide ni, tomodachi ni aimashita.
examples.en: While I was at the library borrowing a book, I ran into a friend.
examples.literalEn: I met my friend while borrowing a book from the library.
examples.naturalEn: While I was at the library borrowing a book, I ran into a friend.

examples.jp: 日本に来たついでに、有名な観光地を訪れたいです。
examples.ja: 日本に来たついでに、有名な観光地を訪れたいです。
examples.romaji: Nihon ni kita tsuide ni, yuumei na kankouchi wo otozuretai desu.
examples.en: While I’m in Japan, I’d like to visit some famous tourist spots.

cloze.after: 、有名な観光地を訪れたいです。

examples.literalEn: While visiting Japan, I'd like to see some famous tourist spots.
examples.naturalEn: While I’m in Japan, I’d like to visit some famous tourist spots.

examples.jp: 映画館に行ったついでに、新作のポスターを見ました。
examples.ja: 映画館に行ったついでに、新作のポスターを見ました。
examples.romaji: Eigakan ni itta tsuide ni, shinsaku no posutaa wo mimashita.
examples.en: While I was at the movie theater, I took a look at the posters for the new releases.

cloze.after: 、新作のポスターを見ました。

examples.literalEn: While going to the movie theater, I saw a poster for a new film.
examples.naturalEn: While I was at the movie theater, I took a look at the posters for the new releases.

notes.nuance: The expression “～ついでに” means “Do something while or after completing another action; ‘while,’ ‘by the way.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～ついでに” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intention or focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the “tsunage” construction (Verb (dictionary form or ta-form) + “tsunagite”, Noun + “no” + “tsunagite”, or Verb-te form + “iru” + “tsunagite”). It is important to choose the correct dictionary form, te-form, and particles.

points.title: ～っけ？ (〜kke?)
points.meaning: Used to express that one is trying to recall some information.
points.explanation: The ～っけ？ grammar point is added at the end of a sentence when the speaker is trying to recall something or confirm a memory. It can be used with verbs, adjectives, or nouns in casual form.
points.short: Used to express that one is trying to recall some information.
points.long: The ～っけ？ grammar point is added at the end of a sentence when the speaker is trying to recall something or confirm a memory. It can be used with verbs, adjectives, or nouns in casual form.
formation: Verb-casual + っけ?, い-Adjective + かったっけ?, な-Adjective/Noun + だっけ?

examples.jp: 彼は何時に来るっけ？
examples.ja: 彼は何時に来るっけ？
examples.romaji: Kare wa nanji ni kuru kke?
examples.en: What time is he coming again?
examples.literalEn: What time is he coming again?
examples.naturalEn: What time is he coming again?

examples.jp: この映画、面白かったっけ？
examples.ja: この映画、面白かったっけ？
examples.romaji: Kono eiga, omoshirokatta kke?

examples.literalEn: Was this movie interesting?
examples.naturalEn: Was this movie any good?

examples.jp: 彼女は学生だっけ？
examples.ja: 彼女は学生だっけ？
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa gakusei dakke?
examples.en: Is she a student?
examples.literalEn: She was a student, right?
examples.naturalEn: Is she a student?

examples.jp: すし屋はどこだっけ？
examples.ja: すし屋はどこだっけ？
examples.romaji: Sushiya wa doko dakke?
examples.en: Where was that sushi restaurant again?

examples.naturalEn: Where was that sushi restaurant again?

notes.nuance: The expression “～っけ？” is used to express that one is trying to recall some information. It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～っけ？” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the “-kke” form (Verb-casual + “kke?”, “i”-adjective + “katta kke?”, “na”-adjective/noun + “dakke?”). It is important to use the dictionary form and “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～っぱい (〜ppai)
points.meaning: Expresses fullness or completeness; 'full', 'full of', 'filled with'.
points.explanation: The ～っぱい grammar point is used to convey that something is filled or packed with something else. Commonly used as 『Noun + でいっぱい』 (e.g., 荷物でいっぱい) to mean 'full of X'.
points.short: Expresses fullness or completeness; 'full', 'full of', 'filled with'.
points.long: The ～っぱい grammar point is used to convey that something is filled or packed with something else. Commonly used as 『Noun + でいっぱい』 (e.g., 荷物でいっぱい) to mean 'full of X'.
formation: Noun + で + いっぱい (Note: written as いっぱい, read as 'ippai')

examples.jp: 部屋が荷物でいっぱいです。
examples.ja: 部屋が荷物でいっぱいです。
examples.romaji: Heya ga nimotsu de ippai desu.
examples.en: The room is full of luggage.
examples.literalEn: The room is full of luggage.
examples.naturalEn: The room is full of luggage.

examples.jp: 彼女は笑顔でいっぱいでした。
examples.ja: 彼女は笑顔でいっぱいでした。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa egao de ippai deshita.
examples.en: She was all smiles.
examples.literalEn: She was full of smiles.
examples.naturalEn: She was all smiles.

examples.jp: 彼は仕事でいっぱいです。
examples.ja: 彼は仕事でいっぱいです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shigoto de ippai desu.
examples.en: He is swamped with work.
examples.literalEn: He is completely busy with work.
examples.naturalEn: He is swamped with work.

examples.jp: 公園は花でいっぱいです。
examples.ja: 公園は花でいっぱいです。
examples.romaji: Kouen wa hana de ippai desu.

examples.naturalEn: The park is full of flowers.

examples.jp: このレモンはとても酸っぱいです。

examples.naturalEn: This lemon is very sour.

examples.ja: 酸っぱいものを食べると顔がしかめる。

examples.naturalEn: When I eat something sour, I grimace.

examples.literalEn: Turn sour apples into a well-balanced dessert.
examples.naturalEn: Turn a sour apple into a well-balanced dessert.

examples.ja: どうしてあなたの態度は酸っぱいの？
examples.romaji: Doushite anata no taido wa suppai no?
examples.en: Why are you being so sour?

cloze.before: どうしてあなたの態度は酸

examples.literalEn: Why is your attitude so sour?
examples.naturalEn: Why are you being so sour?

notes.nuance: The expression “～っぱい” means “fullness or completeness; ‘full,’ ‘full of,’ ‘filled with.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective descriptions and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～っぱい” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of mistakes in the conjugation of the "de" construction (Noun + de + いっぱい (Note: written as いっぱい, read as 'ippai')). It is important to use the dictionary form and the "te" form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～っぱなし (〜ppanashi)
points.meaning: Indicate a state where an action is left as is (unchanged or unfinished).
points.explanation: The ～っぱなし grammar point is used to express that an action happened and was left in that state, unattended or unchanged. It is formed by taking the ます-stem of a verb and adding ～っぱなし.
points.short: Indicate a state where an action is left as is (unchanged or unfinished).
points.long: The ～っぱなし grammar point is used to express that an action happened and was left in that state, unattended or unchanged. It is formed by taking the ます-stem of a verb and adding ～っぱなし.
formation: Verb-ますstem + っぱなし

examples.jp: 窓を開けっぱなしにすると、虫が入ってくる。
examples.ja: 窓を開けっぱなしにすると、虫が入ってくる。

examples.naturalEn: If you leave the window open, bugs will come in.

examples.naturalEn: I left the laundry out to dry, and it got wet in the rain.

examples.jp: 彼はドアを開けっぱなしにして出かけた。
examples.ja: 彼はドアを開けっぱなしにして出かけた。
examples.romaji: Kare wa doa o akeppanashi ni shite dekaketa.

examples.literalEn: He went out leaving the door open.
examples.naturalEn: He went out and left the door open.

examples.ja: テレビをつけっぱなしにして寝てしまった。

examples.literalEn: I fell asleep with the TV left on.
examples.naturalEn: I fell asleep with the TV still on.

notes.nuance: The expression “～っぱなし” indicates “a state where an action is left as is (unchanged or unfinished).” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: Compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～っぱなし” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intention or focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful not to make mistakes in the conjugation of the “-ppa-nashi” form (Verb-masu stem + -ppa-nashi). It is important to use the dictionary form and the “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～つまり (〜tsumari)
points.meaning: Summarizing, restating, or clarifying a point: 'in other words', 'that is to say'.
points.explanation: The ～つまり grammar point is used to restate or clarify in a concise way what has been said. It can be translated as 'in other words', 'that is to say', or 'in short'.
points.short: Summarizing, restating, or clarifying a point: 'in other words', 'that is to say'.
points.long: The ～つまり grammar point is used to restate or clarify in a concise way what has been said. It can be translated as 'in other words', 'that is to say', or 'in short'.
formation: Sentence A + つまり + Sentence B (rephrasing)

examples.jp: 彼は大学の教授です。つまり、専門家です。
examples.ja: 彼は大学の教授です。つまり、専門家です。

examples.literalEn: He is a university professor. In other words, he is an expert.
examples.naturalEn: He is a university professor. In other words, he is an expert.

examples.jp: 今日は土曜日だ。つまり、明日は日曜日だ。
examples.ja: 今日は土曜日だ。つまり、明日は日曜日だ。

examples.naturalEn: Today is Saturday. That means tomorrow is Sunday.

examples.jp: 山田さんは友達のお姉さんです。つまり、私たちの知り合いです。
examples.ja: 山田さんは友達のお姉さんです。つまり、私たちの知り合いです。

examples.literalEn: Ms. Yamada is my friend's older sister. In short, she's someone we know.
examples.naturalEn: Ms. Yamada is my friend’s older sister. In other words, she’s someone we know.

examples.jp: 彼女はフランス出身です。つまり、フランス語が話せます。
examples.ja: 彼女はフランス出身です。つまり、フランス語が話せます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa Furansu shusshin desu. Tsumari, Furansugo ga hanasemasu.
examples.en: She is from France. In other words, she can speak French.

cloze.before: 彼女はフランス出身です。

examples.literalEn: She is from France. In other words, she can speak French.
examples.naturalEn: She is from France. In other words, she can speak French.

notes.nuance: The expression “～つまり” means “Summarizing, restating, or clarifying a point: ‘in other words,’ ‘that is to say.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “~tsuuki” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of mistakes in verb conjugation when using the "connection" structure (Sentence A + "in other words" + Sentence B (rephrasing)). It is important to use the dictionary form, the "te" form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: ～つもりでした (〜tsumori deshita)
points.meaning: Expressing a past intention or plan; 'was planning to', 'meant to'.
points.explanation: The ～つもりでした grammar point is used to express a past intention or plan that did not happen, or a past belief that turned out incorrect. It can be translated as 'was planning to', 'intended to', or 'meant to'.
points.short: Expressing a past intention or plan; 'was planning to', 'meant to'.
points.long: The ～つもりでした grammar point is used to express a past intention or plan that did not happen, or a past belief that turned out incorrect. It can be translated as 'was planning to', 'intended to', or 'meant to'.
formation: Verb-casual (dictionary form) + つもりでした

examples.jp: 昨日は友達に会うつもりでしたが、風邪を引いてしまいました。
examples.ja: 昨日は友達に会うつもりでしたが、風邪を引いてしまいました。
examples.romaji: Kinou wa tomodachi ni au tsumori deshita ga, kaze o hiite shimaimashita.
examples.en: I was planning to meet a friend yesterday, but I caught a cold.

examples.literalEn: I was planning to meet my friend yesterday, but I caught a cold.
examples.naturalEn: I was planning to meet a friend yesterday, but I caught a cold.

examples.literalEn: I intended to watch a movie, but I ran out of time.
examples.naturalEn: I was planning to watch a movie, but I ran out of time.

examples.jp: 彼らが来るつもりでしたが、電話でキャンセルされました。

examples.en: They were planning to come, but they canceled by phone.
chunks: キャンセルされました。

cloze.after: が、電話でキャンセルされました。

examples.literalEn: They were supposed to come, but they canceled by phone.
examples.naturalEn: They were planning to come, but they canceled by phone.

examples.jp: この本を読むつもりでしたが、もう読み終わっていました。
examples.ja: この本を読むつもりでしたが、もう読み終わっていました。
examples.romaji: Kono hon o yomu tsumori deshita ga, mou yomiowatte imashita.
examples.en: I was planning to read this book, but I had already finished it.

cloze.after: が、もう読み終わっていました。

points.title: ～てくれと (〜te kureto)
points.meaning: Quote someone's request (telling someone to do something).
points.explanation: The ～てくれと grammar point is used when quoting a request or command made by someone else. It literally means 'someone said “please do …”'. Typically used as 「～てくれと頼む/言う」 to indicate being asked or told to do something.
points.short: Quote someone's request (telling someone to do something).

points.title: ～てごらん (〜te goran)
points.meaning: Suggest or invite someone to try doing something; 'Why don't you try...'.
points.explanation: The ～てごらん grammar point is used to gently suggest or invite someone to try doing something. It is softer and more casual than ～てみて, and is used among friends or family.

points.title: ですから～ (desu kara)
points.meaning: Expresses reason or cause; 'because', 'since', 'so'.
points.explanation: The ですから grammar point is used to indicate the reason or cause for a statement, often in polite speech. It can be translated as 'because', 'since', or 'so'.
points.short: Expresses reason or cause; 'because', 'since', 'so'.
points.long: The ですから grammar point is used to indicate the reason or cause for a statement, often in polite speech. It can be translated as 'because', 'since', or 'so'.

points.title: ～てはじめて (〜te hajimete)
points.meaning: Realization or action done for the first time; 'only after', 'not until'.
points.explanation: The ～てはじめて grammar point indicates that something is realized or happens for the first time only after another action is completed. It can be translated as 'only after' or 'not until'.
points.short: Realization or action done for the first time; 'only after', 'not until'.
points.long: The ～てはじめて grammar point indicates that something is realized or happens for the first time only after another action is completed. It can be translated as 'only after' or 'not until'.

points.title: ～てほしい (〜te hoshii)
points.meaning: Express a desire for someone else to do something; 'I want you to do...'.
points.explanation: The ～てほしい grammar point is used to express a desire that someone else perform an action. It is formed by attaching ほしい to the て-form of a verb. It can be translated as 'I want you to...' in English.
points.short: Express a desire for someone else to do something; 'I want you to do...'.
points.long: The ～てほしい grammar point is used to express a desire that someone else perform an action. It is formed by attaching ほしい to the て-form of a verb. It can be translated as 'I want you to...' in English.

points.title: ～ても (〜temo)
points.meaning: 'Even if', 'even though', or 'although'.
points.explanation: The ～ても grammar point expresses that even if a certain condition holds, the outcome or situation doesn't change. It can be translated as 'even if' or 'even though'.
points.short: 'Even if', 'even though', or 'although'.
points.long: The ～ても grammar point expresses that even if a certain condition holds, the outcome or situation doesn't change. It can be translated as 'even if' or 'even though'.

points.title: ～ということだ (〜to iu koto da)
points.meaning: Express a conclusion or hearsay; 'I heard', 'it means', 'it can be said'.

points.title: ～というのは (〜to iu no wa)
points.meaning: Used to provide an explanation or definition; 'that is to say...', 'by that, I mean...'.
points.explanation: The ～というのは grammar point is used to provide an explanation or definition of the preceding statement or word. It can be translated as 'that is to say...', 'by that, I mean...', or 'what I mean by...'.
points.short: Used to provide an explanation or definition; 'that is to say...', 'by that, I mean...'.

points.short: Express a comparison with preference; 'rather than', 'more like', 'instead of'.

points.explanation: The ～とく grammar point (from ～ておく) is used to express doing something in advance or preparing for something. It implies you're performing an action now to avoid inconvenience later. It is a casual, colloquial contraction of ～ておく.

points.explanation: The ～ところが grammar point is used to express a contrast or an unexpected outcome. It can be translated as 'however', 'but', or 'even though' in English. It emphasizes a situation that contradicts what was expected.

points.title: ～ところだった (〜tokoro datta)

points.title: ところで (tokorode)
points.meaning: Used for changing the topic or bringing up a new topic; 'by the way', 'speaking of'.

points.title: ～どんなに～ことか (〜donna ni〜koto ka)
points.meaning: Expresses the extent of something or emphasizes the degree of a condition or situation.
points.explanation: The ～どんなに～ことか grammar point is used to emphasize the extent of a condition or circumstance, and to express how much or to what degree something is happening. It is often translated as 'how much', 'how greatly', or 'to what extent' in English. This pattern is usually used with an adjective or verb in a sentence.
points.short: Expresses the extent of something or emphasizes the degree of a condition or situation.
points.long: The ～どんなに～ことか grammar point is used to emphasize the extent of a condition or circumstance, and to express how much or to what degree something is happening. It is often translated as 'how much', 'how greatly', or 'to what extent' in English. This pattern is usually used with an adjective or verb in a sentence.
formation: どんなに + Adjective + ことか, どんなに + Verb + ことか

examples.jp: どんなに疲れたことか、言葉では表せません。
examples.ja: どんなに疲れたことか、言葉では表せません。
examples.romaji: Donna ni tsukareta koto ka, kotoba de wa arawasemasen.
examples.en: I can’t even begin to describe how tired I was.

examples.literalEn: I can't put into words how tired I am.
examples.naturalEn: I can’t even begin to describe how tired I was.

examples.jp: どんなに辛いことか、彼女は毎日頑張って働いています。
examples.ja: どんなに辛いことか、彼女は毎日頑張って働いています。
examples.romaji: Donna ni tsurai koto ka, kanojo wa mainichi ganbatte hataraiteimasu.
examples.en: No matter how difficult it is, she works hard every day.

examples.en: How delightful his success is!
examples.literalEn: How happy his success must be.
examples.naturalEn: How delightful his success is!

examples.jp: どんなに楽しいことか、みんなで旅行に行く。
examples.ja: どんなに楽しいことか、みんなで旅行に行く。
examples.romaji: Donna ni tanoshii koto ka, minna de ryokou ni iku.
examples.en: Going on a trip together is so much fun.

cloze.after: 楽しいことか、みんなで旅行に行く。

examples.literalEn: How fun it is to go on a trip with everyone.
examples.naturalEn: Going on a trip together is so much fun.

notes.nuance: This expression, “～どんなに～ことか,” “expresses the extent of something or emphasizes the degree of a condition or situation.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, the construction “～どんなに～ことか” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the "-koto ka" construction (e.g., "donna ni + adjective + koto ka," "donna ni + verb + koto ka"). It is important to use the dictionary form and "te" form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: どんなに～ても (donna ni ~ temo)
points.meaning: Expresses 'no matter how much' or 'even if'; emphasizes the degree of a situation.
points.explanation: The どんなに～ても grammar point is used to emphasize the degree of a situation or condition, often translated as 'no matter how much' or 'even if' in English. It can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, and な-adjectives.
points.short: Expresses 'no matter how much' or 'even if'; emphasizes the degree of a situation.
points.long: The どんなに～ても grammar point is used to emphasize the degree of a situation or condition, often translated as 'no matter how much' or 'even if' in English. It can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, and な-adjectives.
formation: どんなに + Verb-てform + も, どんなに + い-Adjective-てform + も, どんなに + な-Adjective + でも

examples.en: No matter how much I study, there are still things I don’t understand.

notes.nuance: The expression “どんなに～ても” means “Expresses ‘no matter how much’ or ‘even if’; emphasizes the degree of a situation.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “doko ni mo ~te mo” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the "-nani-mo" construction (e.g., "donna ni + Verb-te-form + mo," "donna ni + i-adjective-te-form + mo," "donna ni + na-adjective + demo"). It is important to use the dictionary form, the "te" form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: ～ないことはない (〜nai koto wa nai)
points.meaning: Express the idea that 'it's not that it's impossible' or 'it's not that it cannot be done'.
points.explanation: The ～ないことはない grammar point is used to express that something is not impossible, or not that it cannot be done. It creates a softer, more indirect way of saying that something is possible or can be done, but not necessarily easy or preferred.
points.short: Express the idea that 'it's not that it's impossible' or 'it's not that it cannot be done'.
points.long: The ～ないことはない grammar point is used to express that something is not impossible, or not that it cannot be done. It creates a softer, more indirect way of saying that something is possible or can be done, but not necessarily easy or preferred.
formation: Verb-ない form + ことはない

notes.nuance: The expression “～ないことはない” conveys the idea that “it’s not that it’s impossible” or “it’s not that it cannot be done.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, “～ないことはない” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful not to make mistakes in the conjugation of the "-nai" form followed by "-koto wa nai." It is important to use the dictionary form and the "te" form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～ないと (〜nai to)
points.meaning: Express a condition; 'if... not', 'unless', 'must'.
points.explanation: The ～ないと grammar point is used to express a condition, focusing on the negative consequences if the action is not performed. It can be translated as 'if... not', 'unless', or 'must' in English. The formation is simply attaching ないと to the negative form of a verb.
points.short: Express a condition; 'if... not', 'unless', 'must'.
points.long: The ～ないと grammar point is used to express a condition, focusing on the negative consequences if the action is not performed. It can be translated as 'if... not', 'unless', or 'must' in English. The formation is simply attaching ないと to the negative form of a verb.
formation: Verb-negative form + ないと

points.title: ～なぜなら (〜nazenara)
points.meaning: Express a reason or explanation; 'because', 'the reason is'.
points.explanation: The ～なぜなら grammar point is used to provide a reason or explanation for a preceding statement or situation. It can be translated as 'because' or 'the reason is' in English. It is often followed by から or だから to emphasize the reason or cause.
points.short: Express a reason or explanation; 'because', 'the reason is'.
points.long: The ～なぜなら grammar point is used to provide a reason or explanation for a preceding statement or situation. It can be translated as 'because' or 'the reason is' in English. It is often followed by から or だから to emphasize the reason or cause.

points.title: ～など (〜nado)
points.meaning: Indicates a non-exhaustive list of examples; 'such as', 'things like', 'among others'.
points.explanation: The ～など grammar point is used to give a non-exhaustive list of examples, meaning the mentioned items are only some of many possibilities. It can be translated as 'such as', 'things like', or 'among others' in English. This grammar point can be used with nouns.
points.short: Indicates a non-exhaustive list of examples; 'such as', 'things like', 'among others'.
points.long: The ～など grammar point is used to give a non-exhaustive list of examples, meaning the mentioned items are only some of many possibilities. It can be translated as 'such as', 'things like', or 'among others' in English. This grammar point can be used with nouns.

points.title: ～なんか (〜nanka)
points.meaning: Expresses the idea of 'things like' or 'something like', used for listing examples or downplaying something.
points.explanation: The ～なんか grammar point is used for listing examples by indicating 'things like' or 'something like'. It can also be used to downplay or devalue something, making it seem less important or less significant than it really is.
points.short: Expresses the idea of 'things like' or 'something like', used for listing examples or downplaying something.

points.title: ～において (〜ni oite)
points.meaning: Indicates the place, time, or context where an action or situation takes place.
points.explanation: The ～において grammar point is used to indicate where an action or situation occurs. It can often be translated as 'in', 'at', or 'on' in English. In some cases, it can also express a specific context or aspect. This grammar point can be used with verbs, adjectives, and nouns.
points.short: Indicates the place, time, or context where an action or situation takes place.
points.long: The ～において grammar point is used to indicate where an action or situation occurs. It can often be translated as 'in', 'at', or 'on' in English. In some cases, it can also express a specific context or aspect. This grammar point can be used with verbs, adjectives, and nouns.
formation: Noun (Place/Time/Context) + において

examples.jp: 科学の分野において、研究が日々進んでいます。

examples.naturalEn: During early childhood, children learn things with great enthusiasm.

examples.naturalEn: That is one possible option for the future.

notes.nuance: The expression “～において” means “Indicates the place, time, or context where an action or situation takes place.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～において” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of mistakes in conjugation when using the “-ni” construction (Noun (Place/Time/Context) + “-ni oite”). It is important to use the dictionary form, the “te” form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: ～にかわって (〜ni kawatte)
points.meaning: Expresses 'in place of', 'on behalf of', or 'instead of'.
points.explanation: The ～にかわって grammar point is used to express that someone or something is acting in place of, on behalf of, or instead of someone or something else. Typically used with nouns (e.g., 人, 会社, etc.).
points.short: Expresses 'in place of', 'on behalf of', or 'instead of'.
points.long: The ～にかわって grammar point is used to express that someone or something is acting in place of, on behalf of, or instead of someone or something else. Typically used with nouns (e.g., 人, 会社, etc.).
formation: Noun + にかわって

examples.jp: 彼が病気なので、私が会議に出席することになりました。私が彼にかわって会議に出席します。
examples.ja: 彼が病気なので、私が会議に出席することになりました。私が彼にかわって会議に出席します。
examples.romaji: Kare ga byouki na no de, watashi ga kaigi ni shusseki suru koto ni narimashita. Watashi ga kare ni kawatte kaigi ni shusseki shimasu.
examples.en: Since he is sick, I will be attending the meeting. I will attend the meeting in his place.
chunks: 出席することになりました。

cloze.before: 彼が病気なので、私が会議に出席することになりました。私が彼

examples.literalEn: He is sick, so I will attend the meeting. I will attend the meeting on his behalf.
examples.naturalEn: Since he is sick, I will be attending the meeting. I will attend the meeting in his place.

examples.jp: 母は忙しいので、私が母にかわって料理を作ります。
examples.ja: 母は忙しいので、私が母にかわって料理を作ります。
examples.romaji: Haha wa isogashii no de, watashi ga haha ni kawatte ryouri wo tsukurimasu.

examples.naturalEn: My mother is busy, so I’ll cook in her place.

examples.romaji: Kondo no ryokou wa imouto ni kawatte, watashi ga issho ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I’ll be going on this trip instead of my younger sister.

examples.naturalEn: I’ll be going on this trip instead of my younger sister.

examples.jp: 先生が出張中でいないので、助手が先生にかわってクラスを担当します。
examples.ja: 先生が出張中でいないので、助手が先生にかわってクラスを担当します。
examples.romaji: Sensei ga shucchou chuu de inai no de, joshu ga sensei ni kawatte kurasu wo tantou shimasu.

examples.naturalEn: Since the teacher is away on a business trip, the teaching assistant will be leading the class in the teacher’s place.

notes.nuance: The expression “～にかわって” means “in place of,” “on behalf of,” or “instead of.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, “～にかわって” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of mistakes in conjugation when using the “in place of” construction (Noun + ni kawatte). It is important to use the dictionary form, the “te” form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: ～にしては (〜ni shite wa)
points.meaning: Express 'for' or 'considering' in the sense of being unusual or unexpected.
points.explanation: The ～にしては grammar point is used to express that something is unusual or unexpected considering a specific condition or context. It can be translated as 'for' or 'considering' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
points.short: Express 'for' or 'considering' in the sense of being unusual or unexpected.
points.long: The ～にしては grammar point is used to express that something is unusual or unexpected considering a specific condition or context. It can be translated as 'for' or 'considering' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + にしては, い-Adjective + にしては, な-Adjective + にしては, Noun + にしては

examples.jp: 彼女は初心者にしては、上手に水泳ができる。
examples.ja: 彼女は初心者にしては、上手に水泳ができる。

examples.naturalEn: He is very calm for someone his age.

examples.ja: あの人は外国人にしては、日本語がうまい。

examples.naturalEn: For a foreigner, that person speaks Japanese quite well.

notes.nuance: The expression “～にしては” means “Express ‘for’ or ‘considering’ in the sense of being unusual or unexpected.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～にしては” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent or focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the “-ni shite” construction (Verb-casual + -ni shite, i-adjective + -ni shite, na-adjective + -ni shite, noun + -ni shite). It is important to use the dictionary form or “te” form correctly and choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～にしても (〜ni shitemo)
points.meaning: Expresses 'even if', 'no matter', 'regardless of'.
points.explanation: The ～にしても grammar point is used to express that even if a certain condition is true or a certain situation occurs, the outcome will not change. It can be translated as 'even if', 'no matter', or 'regardless of' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
points.short: Expresses 'even if', 'no matter', 'regardless of'.
points.long: The ～にしても grammar point is used to express that even if a certain condition is true or a certain situation occurs, the outcome will not change. It can be translated as 'even if', 'no matter', or 'regardless of' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + にしても, い-Adjective + にしても, な-Adjective + だにしても, Noun + だにしても

notes.nuance: The expression “～にしても” means “even if,” “no matter,” or “regardless of.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～にしても” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent or focus.

points.title: ～について (〜ni tsuite)
points.meaning: Expressing 'about', 'concerning', or 'regarding'.
points.explanation: The ～について grammar point is used to express 'about', 'concerning', or 'regarding' a certain topic or subject. It is often used in both casual and formal contexts. The formation is simple – just add について after the noun that represents the topic you are discussing.
points.short: Expressing 'about', 'concerning', or 'regarding'.
points.long: The ～について grammar point is used to express 'about', 'concerning', or 'regarding' a certain topic or subject. It is often used in both casual and formal contexts. The formation is simple – just add について after the noun that represents the topic you are discussing.

points.title: ～にとって (〜ni totte)

points.short: Express the meaning 'for', 'to', 'from the perspective of'.

notes.nuance: The expression “～ばかり” means “only,” “nothing but,” “always,” or “just.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～ばかり” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the “-bakkari” construction (Verb-masu stem + bakkari, i-adjective + bakkari, na-adjective + bakkari, noun + bakkari). It is important to use the dictionary form and “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～ばかりか (〜bakarika) ～も (mo)
points.meaning: Not only... but also; more than just; not just
points.explanation: The grammar point ～ばかりか ～も is used to emphasize that something is not limited to only one thing, but also includes another thing. It can be translated as 'not only... but also', 'more than just', or 'not just' in English. This expression is typically used with verbs, adjectives, and nouns.
points.short: Not only... but also; more than just; not just

It can be translated as 'not only... but also', 'more than just', or 'not just' in English. This expression is typically used with verbs, adjectives, and nouns.

points.title: ～はずだ (〜hazu da)
points.meaning: Expresses an expectation, 'should' or 'it is supposed to'.
points.explanation: The ～はずだ grammar point is used to express an expectation or belief that something is true, even if it has not been confirmed. It can be translated as 'should', 'it is supposed to', or 'ought to' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.

points.title: ～ば～のに (〜ba 〜noni)

It can be translated as 'if only' or 'wish' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.

points.title: ～ふりをする (〜furi wo suru)

points.explanation: The ～べきだ grammar point is used to express a sense of obligation or to indicate something that should be done. In modern Japanese, it is almost always used with verbs in the dictionary form. In English, it can be translated as 'should' or 'ought to'.

points.title: もしも～なら (moshimo ~ nara)
points.meaning: Express a hypothetical condition or situation; 'if', 'in case', 'suppose'.
points.explanation: The もしも～なら grammar point is used to express a hypothetical condition or situation, often with a sense of uncertainty. It can be translated as 'if', 'in case', or 'suppose'. The formation varies slightly based on whether it is used with a verb, an い-adjective, a な-adjective, or a noun.
points.short: Express a hypothetical condition or situation; 'if', 'in case', 'suppose'.

points.meaning: Not showing any sign or intention to do something.
points.explanation: The ～ようとしない grammar point indicates that someone is not showing any sign or intention of doing an action. It is used to express a refusal or unwillingness to do something. It is formed by using the volitional form of a verb followed by としない.

points.title: ～ようになった (〜you ni natta)
points.meaning: Express an event or state that became possible; 'became able to', 'started to', 'now can'.
points.explanation: The ～ようになった grammar point is used to express that an event, ability, or state has become possible or started to occur. It can be translated as 'became able to', 'started to', or 'now can' in English. Usually this is used with verbs in their dictionary or potential form (e.g., 食べられるようになった).
points.short: Express an event or state that became possible; 'became able to', 'started to', 'now can'.
points.long: The ～ようになった grammar point is used to express that an event, ability, or state has become possible or started to occur. It can be translated as 'became able to', 'started to', or 'now can' in English. Usually this is used with verbs in their dictionary or potential form (e.g., 食べられるようになった).

points.title: ～らしい (〜rashii)

points.explanation: The ～らしい grammar point is used to indicate that the information provided is based on hearsay or an indirect source. points.title: ～られた (〜rareta)
points.meaning: Express a passive action, 'was/were', 'has/have been'.
points.explanation: The ～られた grammar point is used to express a passive action or situation. It is formed by conjugating the verb into its passive form in the past tense, which can be translated into English as 'was/were' or 'has/have been'. This grammar is used in situations where the subject is affected by an action rather than performing the action itself.

points.title: ～ている (〜te iru)
points.meaning: Expresses a continuing action or a resulting state; 'is ~ing', 'has been', 'has'.
points.explanation: The ～ている grammar point is used to describe a continuing or repeated action, or the result/state of a completed action. Depending on the context, it can be translated as 'is ~ing', 'has been ~ed', or simply 'has/are/is'. In passive contexts (e.g., 食べられている, 開けられている), it shows that something has been done and remains in that state. With intransitive or non-passive verbs, it shows an ongoing or resultant state (e.g., 寝込んでいる, 終わっている).
points.short: Expresses a continuing action or a resulting state; 'is ~ing', 'has been', 'has'.
points.long: The ～ている grammar point is used to describe a continuing or repeated action, or the result/state of a completed action. Depending on the context, it can be translated as 'is ~ing', 'has been ~ed', or simply 'has/are/is'. In passive contexts (e.g., 食べられている, 開けられている), it shows that something has been done and remains in that state. With intransitive or non-passive verbs, it shows an ongoing or resultant state (e.g., 寝込んでいる, 終わっている).

points.title: ～んだって (〜n datte)
points.meaning: Conveys information heard from someone else; 'I heard', 'They said'.
points.explanation: The ～んだって grammar point is used to relay information the speaker has heard from someone else. It's a casual way of quoting what was said, effectively combining explanatory のだ (んだ) with the informal quoting particle って. It can be translated as 'I heard...' or 'They said...'.
points.short: Conveys information heard from someone else; 'I heard', 'They said'.
points.long: The ～んだって grammar point is used to relay information the speaker has heard from someone else. It's a casual way of quoting what was said, effectively combining explanatory のだ (んだ) with the informal quoting particle って. It can be translated as 'I heard...' or 'They said...'.

points.title: ～んだもん (〜nda mon)
points.meaning: Used to convey a sense of justification; 'because', 'that's why', 'it's just that'.

It can be translated as 'because', 'that's why', or 'it's just that' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
points.short: Used to convey a sense of justification; 'because', 'that's why', 'it's just that'.

points.title: ～上げる (〜ageru)

points.title: ～切れない (～kirenai)
points.meaning: Expresses inability to completely finish or do something.
points.explanation: The ～切れない grammar point is used to express the inability to fully complete, finish, or do something. It is formed by attaching 切れない to the stem of a verb. It often implies that some portion of the action is done, but finishing it entirely is not possible for some reason.

examples.romaji: Kesshite akiramenai de, saigo made ganbarimashou.
examples.en: Never give up—let’s keep trying until the very end.

cloze.after: 諦めないで、最後までがんばりましょう。

examples.literalEn: Never give up and keep trying until the end.
examples.naturalEn: Never give up—let’s keep trying until the very end.

examples.jp: 彼女は決して嘘をつかない人です。
examples.ja: 彼女は決して嘘をつかない人です。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa kesshite uso o tsukanai hito desu.
examples.en: She is someone who never lies.
examples.literalEn: She is a person who never lies.
examples.naturalEn: She is someone who never lies.

examples.jp: 彼は質を維持するために、決して妥協しない人だ。
examples.ja: 彼は質を維持するために、決して妥協しない人だ。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shitsu o iji suru tame ni, kesshite dakyou shinai hito da.
examples.en: He is someone who never compromises when it comes to maintaining quality.

cloze.before: 彼は質を維持するために、

examples.literalEn: He is a person who never compromises in order to maintain quality.
examples.naturalEn: He is someone who never compromises when it comes to maintaining quality.

examples.jp: 彼は決して折れることがない強い意志をもっている。
examples.ja: 彼は決して折れることがない強い意志をもっている。
examples.romaji: Kare wa kesshite oreru koto ga nai tsuyoi ishi o motte iru.
examples.en: He has a strong will that never wavers.

cloze.after: 折れることがない強い意志をもっている。

examples.literalEn: He has a strong will that never breaks.
examples.naturalEn: He has a strong will that never wavers.

examples.jp: この素晴らしい思い出は、決して忘れることはできない。
examples.ja: この素晴らしい思い出は、決して忘れることはできない。
examples.romaji: Kono subarashii omoide wa, kesshite wasureru koto wa dekinai
examples.en: I will never forget this wonderful memory.

cloze.before: この素晴らしい思い出は、
cloze.after: 忘れることはできない。

examples.literalEn: I can never forget these wonderful memories.
examples.naturalEn: I will never forget this wonderful memory.

notes.nuance: This expression, “決して～ない,” is used to express “never,” “by no means,” or “not at all” when negating a statement. It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N3 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “決して～ない” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the “決して + Verb (negative form)” construction. It is important to use the dictionary form and the “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.
